name: Coffee Hunters
about: Specialty cafes, pour-over tips, roasters and the best iced latte in the heat. Honest reviews, no paid placements.

stories.author: p08
stories.text: New single origin on the menu at my Al Quoz bar. Notes of jasmine and peach.

stories.author: p03
stories.text: Coffee and cake pairing night, Downtown, this Thursday. Limited seats!

stories.author: p09
stories.text: Cold brew tasting done. Cold brew wins for summer, no argument.

posts.author: p08
posts.text: Pour over tip of the week: bloom your grounds for 45 seconds with just enough water to wet them. The gas escapes, the flavour opens up. Try it tomorrow morning.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: 45 seconds feels like forever when the kettle is singing. Worth it, though.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pastry brain says this is like proofing dough. Let the gas out, then go.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I tried it this morning and the cup tastes clearer. Thank you, Yusuf!

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Bloom time for light roasts versus dark roasts, is it different? Asking for my new beans.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Coffee nerd question: what grind size do you use for a V60 at home?

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @hannah_b medium-fine, like sea salt. Adjust by taste, not by the book.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Running fuel and coffee nerdery, the perfect combo. Going to try it before my run.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: My kettle is too slow, so I bloom while the water cools a little. Works fine.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim coach needs his espresso to start the day, so the bloom tip is noted.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy lies next to me during the coffee ritual now. He's a true coffee dog.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @mariam_s the puppy gets water, not coffee, please. The rule stands.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Bloom then pour in circles, slow and steady. My grandmother's tea technique, almost.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: I'll try it on the balcony this morning. Hope the neighbours don't notice the kettle.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good tip. The bloom step is the one most people skip, and it shows in the cup.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Scale and timer, that's my advice. Weighing the water changes everything.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Weighing is the nerdy step I finally accept. Got a cheap scale yesterday.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A little cheap scale is a big life upgrade for a runner who loves coffee, sure.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good coffee after a cold swim is the reward I keep dreaming about.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Tell me how it goes, I want the feedback from everyone in the group.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Will report on the flavour. I'm expecting an upgrade from my usual pour.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Please share the beans you use for the bloom test, it helps with the comparison.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the bloom tip. The water part, obviously, he's a fan.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Coffee is my favourite morning ritual. Thank you for turning it into a science.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Going to try it tomorrow with my favourite Ethiopian beans. Report incoming.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Bloom, pour, sip, repeat. Yalla, coffee lovers, let's make the group the best in town ☕

posts.author: p06
posts.text: Cold brew versus iced latte in the summer heat. I know which one wins for flavour, but my wallet votes for cold brew since it lasts longer. What is your pick?

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Cold brew, every time. Slow extraction tastes sweeter with less bitterness.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Iced latte for the milk and the cake pairing. Cold brew is too strong for me with sweets.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cold brew in a bottle is a lifesaver for the commute. Keep one in the fridge.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Iced latte with oat milk is my summer ritual. The milk makes it feel like a treat.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'm team cold brew with a splash of tonic, very Dubai in the summer.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Cold brew before a run, not sure about the stomach. Iced latte after the run.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would pick the milk. He licked the foam off my cup this morning, shameless.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Iced espresso tonic is my pick. Fizzy, bold and refreshing after the sea.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Cold brew costs less per cup when you batch it at home. My wallet thanks me too.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: @anjali_rao that's the honest answer. Batch brew is the winner for the budget.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Batch brew with good beans is the best money you'll ever spend, I promise.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Try a cold brew with vanilla syrup and a drop of cream. It tastes like dessert.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Vanilla in cold brew is a cheat code. Layla, you are right.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: I'd never thought about the tonic, Hannah. Will try it this weekend.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Tonic is an acquired taste, but once you're in, there's no going back.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Cold brew stays smooth in the fridge for days. Good for a busy week.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Cold brew with ice cubes made of coffee, no dilution. A clever trick from a friend.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Coffee ice cubes for the puppy's water bowl? No, I'm kidding. Maybe.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @mariam_s please not, the puppy must stay on water, I beg you.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Honest poll result so far: cold brew leads, iced latte is close behind.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Let's see the final result by the end of the week. Cold brew is my bet.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Iced latte forever for me, I need the sweetness to survive the heat.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: A fair debate. Both are good, the best is the one you enjoy right now.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good answer, Tomasz. Enjoy the coffee and the sun, whichever you pick.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Summer, iced, and friends. My kind of coffee chat. Yalla ☕

posts.author: p03
posts.text: Review: a Downtown cafe with a lemon tart and a flat white that tastes like a sunny afternoon. Service was calm, the seats are comfortable, and the price is fair for the area.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Lemon tart plus flat white is my ideal Downtown order. The tart base is crisp, nice.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Which cafe is it? The seats sound perfect for a long Saturday brunch with laptops.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Price fair for Downtown is a rare compliment. Good find, Layla.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Calm service is underrated. The staff there remember your name after two visits.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Comfortable seats and power sockets make it a work spot for me. Going this Monday.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A flat white after a run is my favourite. Glad the place has proper cups and not paper.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: The lemon tart is my weak spot. Sharp, sweet, and the pastry is buttery.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Lemon, coffee and sunshine. Sounds like the perfect Dubai afternoon to me.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy-friendly? I'm asking for a friend, who is a very small puppy.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: @mariam_s the terrace is dog-friendly, but ask first. The staff are kind.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Flat white with a good milk texture is an art. Let me know if they steam it well.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @yusuf_d I'll be the judge of milk. Will report the steam quality on Monday.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good thing you're thorough, Sara. The milk deserves a proper review.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Afternoon light through the windows is gorgeous. Great for photos and for daydreaming.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Downtown is busy, but this place feels like a little secret. Keep it quiet, please.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Keeping it quiet is impossible when the tart is this good, sorry Hannah.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Honest review, five stars for the vibe and four for the parking. Traffic is brutal.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Parking Downtown is a challenge, use the metro and walk through the mall. Easy.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: I'll bring the puppy to the terrace this weekend, if it is open and happy with dogs.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Puppy visit would make my week. Please send a photo with the tart.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A good review is one that makes you want to visit. Mission accomplished, Layla.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Going this weekend for the tart. Thanks for the detailed review, very helpful.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The fair price and calm vibe, the two things I look for. Good call.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Tart plus flat white equals a perfect Saturday, I agree with everything here.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'll bring the team next Thursday for a proper lemon tart session.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Hot take: the best coffee in Dubai is served in a small corner shop, not a big chain. The owner remembers your order and the espresso never tastes burnt. Fight me.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Small shops win every time. Less pressure on the beans, more care in the cup.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I agree, the corner bakery shop feels like home, and the coffee is consistent.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Chains have their place for speed, but the small shops are where the magic is.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: No fight from me. Corner shop coffee is the one I miss when I travel.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Small shops are where founders go to think. Fewer people, better ideas, better coffee.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Corner shop coffee after an early run is a special thing. The staff knows the runner.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy loves the corner shop owner, he gives him a biscuit every time. Small shops are the best.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Big chains are consistent, but small shops are personal. Both have a place in the city.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Shops that roast in house tend to have better coffee. Ask where the beans come from.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @yusuf_d and I think your place counts as a corner shop, so I'm biased.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Thank you, Tomasz. The corner shop is a family business and we love every customer.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A family-run cafe is the heart of any neighbourhood. Keep supporting them, friends.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Make a list of your favourite small shops and share it, let's build a map together.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Yes, a shared list would be amazing. Please include the good seats and the good wifi.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Wifi is important for the founders. Add the password status to the list, not the password.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Coffee after the group run should be on the map. Include the ones with cold water.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Cold water at the counter is the first thing a good coffee shop offers. Keep that in mind.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Dog water bowls too, please. The corner shop test: do they have a water bowl for pups?

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Yes, that's a great test. A shop with a dog bowl is a shop that cares.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I'll start a list today and share it in the group. Let's see how many corners we can find.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Great idea. A map of corner shops will help the small roasters too.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pastry plus coffee plus corner shop equals my favourite afternoon. Count me in.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Sending my list soon. Thanks for starting this, Tomasz.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Corner shop lovers unite. Yalla, let's support them all 🎧

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Hear, hear! Small shops for the win, and the best coffee for everyone.

posts.author: p09
posts.text: Cold brew tasting at home: four beans, three brew times, one winner. Notes: the Kenyan coffee was bright, the Colombian was chocolate and calm. Full results coming soon.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Kenyan bright and Colombian chocolate is a classic pairing. Nice tasting, Hannah.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Chocolate notes plus a slice of cake, the Colombian is my winner too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Brew time for the cold brew, how long did you steep? Twelve hours?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Four beans and three brew times, the science is strong. Results with a scoring sheet?

comments.author: p06
comments.text: A scoring sheet would be great. Acidity, sweetness, body, aftertaste, the classic five.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Cold brew is my runner's fuel. Chocolate and calm is exactly what I need after a hard session.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy gets a cold water bowl during every tasting. He is very professional about it.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Bright and fruity for summer, chocolate for winter. A year-round coffee plan.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @hannah_b did you use filtered water? Water makes a huge difference in cold brew.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Filtered water, yes, and the same batch of beans. Controlled test, I promise.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Hannah the founder with a lab notebook. Next thing, a coffee startup pitch deck.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ha, a coffee startup pitch deck would be lovely, with pastries in the appendix.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Hannah, please share the notebook pages. I'm curious about the extraction ratio.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Extraction ratio is the number I always forget. Write it on the bag, people.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: I'll try the Colombian at home this weekend, cold brew for the family.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Cold brew for the post-run cool-down, the plan is set. Thanks for the tasting notes.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good tasting notes, Hannah. The scoring sheet will be the most useful thing you post.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Please post the grind size too. It's the variable that people always forget.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is now asking for cold brew. The answer is still no, sweetheart.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @mariam_s water only, he'll survive without the coffee, I promise you.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll bake a coffee cake to go with the next tasting. Deal?

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Deal, Layla. The cake is the official sponsor of the tasting.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Looking forward to the full results. Keep the scoring honest, please.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Yalla, let's make the tasting a monthly thing in the group. Good energy here.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Monthly tasting night sounds perfect. Count me in, I'll bring the playlist.

posts.author: p01
posts.text: Brewing equipment question: is a moka pot worth it for everyday coffee in Dubai, or should I invest in a proper espresso machine for the flat? Budget is modest.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A moka pot is excellent for the budget. Strong, simple and reliable, I roast with one at home.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Moka pot for daily, pour-over for weekends. That's my setup and it works well.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Get a moka pot first, learn the basics, then decide if you need the espresso machine.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Espresso machines are fun but expensive to maintain. Moka pots are very forgiving.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I went with a moka and a cheap grinder. Best purchase of the year for my team mornings.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A moka pot on the stove is perfect for a runner's breakfast, quick and strong.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the moka pot. He likes the sound of the bubbling, honestly.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Moka is great, but make sure the water doesn't boil too hard. Keeps the taste clean.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Grinder matters more than the machine. A good grinder with a cheap brewer beats the reverse.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @anjali_rao that's the advice I needed. Grinder first, then the brewer.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Exactly. Burr grinder, even if it's a basic model, changes the whole cup.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I still use a hand grinder in the flat. It's slow but therapeutic, like kneading dough.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Hand grinders are a workout, but the coffee is worth the arm pain. Respect, Layla.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Moka pot with fresh beans, from a roaster nearby, is the simplest pleasure in life.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Cleaning the moka pot matters too. Rinse, dry, and no soap, the old rule.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: No soap in the moka, yes, the coffee oils are part of the flavour. Good reminder.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's do a moka pot comparison at the next tasting night, I'll bring three brands.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will supervise the comparison from the rug, as usual.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Bring the beans and I'll bring the roast notes. Let's make it a proper night.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Good plan, and the moka comparison will help the newcomers a lot.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Yes, and cake. Always cake. Everything is better with cake.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thanks everyone. I'll buy a moka pot this weekend and start from there.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck Sara. Your first cup will be a little rough, that's part of the fun.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Enjoy the journey, and remember to smile at your first cup, it's a milestone ☕

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Descale the moka pot every few months if your water is hard. Dubai water needs care.

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Coffee in the afternoon, do you have a cut-off time? Mine is 3pm, after that I am staring at the ceiling at midnight. Anyone else hit the same wall?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: My cut-off is noon for runs. Even an afternoon espresso keeps me up, so I switched to decaf.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: My cut-off is 2pm. Puppy needs a long afternoon nap and so do I, honestly.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'm a coffee man, so my cut-off is a myth. I drink decaf after 4 and sleep fine.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pastry chef at 5am means my cut-off is 6pm. Bread needs me to be sharp at dawn.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Caffeine half-life is around five hours, so an afternoon coffee does reach bed time.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: I drink cold brew late and still sleep. It's all about your body, I think.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Decaf is a surprisingly good cup now. The better roasts make a big difference.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Startup life means coffee at 9pm. My cut-off is basically a dream, sadly.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim training makes me sleepy after eight, so I stop caffeine by two. Recovery matters.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @omar_q that's a smart rule. Maybe I'll copy your two o'clock stop.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Try a light roast after noon, it's lower in caffeine per cup. A small trick.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Light roasts actually have a bit more caffeine by weight, a common myth. Just so you know.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy does not drink coffee, but he sleeps like a champion. Life lessons from dogs.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Herbal tea after three, my secret. Mint and lemon, the sleep is much better.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Herbal tea is underrated in this heat. Cold mint tea with lemon is my afternoon ritual.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Cold mint tea is a great alternative. I'll try it on the balcony this summer.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Coffee at three is a choice, not a rule. Enjoy it and sleep well.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks everyone, this thread is the best sleep advice I've had all year.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Sleep is the real recovery. Coffee is a bonus, so keep the cut-off honest.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Agreed, sleep is the thing I protect the most. Good luck with the cut-off, Anjali.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll stop arguing about caffeine and keep roasting. My sleep is fine, honest.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Well said. Sleep is important for humans and dogs alike, wise words from the puppy.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Let's keep the afternoon coffee for the friends who need it, and the tea for the rest.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Good plan, Layla. I'll do the mint tea after three from today. Thanks all 🌿

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Tea at the office is my compromise, a hot mint brew even in the summer heat.

posts.author: p10
posts.text: Cafe etiquette rant: please don't camp at a two-seater for four hours with one latte. Share the space, order something else, and say thank you to the staff. Simple.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Yes! The staff are juggling a full bar and a full queue. Respect the small spaces.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: As a cafe owner, the four hour latte is a real challenge. Please buy a second item, thank you.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: I work from cafes often. I order a snack every two hours. Fair deal for everyone.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Long sessions are fine when the cafe is quiet. Busy hours need turnover, simple.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Say thank you to the barista, every time. It takes two seconds and changes the whole vibe.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Laptop with headphones at a two-seater is the worst. Please move to the big table.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I don't camp anywhere. Quick coffee, quick run, quick goodbye. Fair game.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would be asked to leave any cafe that has a laptop and a latte fight. Tragic.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Cafes that charge for the wifi after an hour are a whole other conversation. Hmm.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @sarak fair, but a clear time limit on the sign helps everyone. Polite and clear.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Staff should be able to say we have a queue, nicely. It's their business too.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Exactly. A friendly reminder goes a long way. Most people just forget.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good rule: buy a second item every hour and nobody complains. Simple.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Oat latte and a cookie for a three-hour meeting. That's my rule, and it works.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Quiet music, good seats, and a friendly team, that's the perfect cafe for me.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Mornings are the worst for camping, the commuters need the table. Be mindful.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Dogs at a cafe must also be well behaved, same principle. Thank you Omar for the reminder.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's make a cafe etiquette card for the group. Five simple rules to share.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Yes please, and keep it short. Nobody reads a long rule list in a cafe.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Rule one: say thank you. Rule two: the big table is for groups. Rule three, cake.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Rule four: the barista is not a waiter, a tip jar is enough. Hmm, I'll hush now.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Rule five: bring a good mood. The cafe smells better with a smile in it.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good list. I'll put it on the cafe window in my head, very wise.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: We're a group of coffee lovers with good manners, what a lovely community.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Keep the cafes happy, and the coffee will keep us happy. Balance.

posts.author: p05
posts.text: Dog friendly cafe check: I visited a new cafe in Mirdif with a shaded terrace, a water bowl for pups, and a barista who asked my puppy's name. Five stars from both of us.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A barista who asks the puppy's name is a barista who deserves a tip. Excellent service.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Name of the cafe please, I'm in Mirdif too. Need a cafe with a dog bowl near home.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Shaded terrace plus a dog bowl is a great combo. The puppy is lucky to have you.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Name the puppy in the post, please. I want to know the official name for the group.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good to see dog-friendly coffee places growing. Keep these reviews coming, Mariam.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Mirdif is getting cafes that care about pets. Let's celebrate the neighbourhood.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A water bowl at a cafe is the best sign of a good owner. Respect to that team.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Puppy with a coffee shop name tag, cutest content of the week. Thank you Mariam.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I'll run to this cafe with my dog next Sunday, if the terrace is open early.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: @ravi_menon open at 8am on weekends, the terrace is the best spot in the morning.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee shops that welcome dogs are good for business too. More people sit longer.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dog water bowl and a cake display, the perfect balance of kind and tempting.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thanks for the review, Mariam. I'll bring my cat to the window seat, she loves the view.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cat in the window seat is a whole vibe. A cat cafe would be a hit in Mirdif.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Good review, the puppy looks happy in the photo. Yalla, more of these stories.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Puppy name please. Hashtag puppy goals, I can't stop looking at that tail.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A friendly barista and a dog bowl. Sounds like a community to me.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I'll share the review in the running group too, the dogs and the runners need more coffee spots.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Thank you, everyone. The puppy's name is Biscuit, and he is now a cafe regular.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Biscuit the cafe regular, a great name for a great dog. Welcome to the team.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Biscuit is perfect for a pastry-loving puppy. Let's make a Biscuit menu item.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Biscuit is the best name I've heard all week. Sending the group a high five.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Biscuit and Mango would be great friends, maybe a dog and cat meetup at the window.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: A cafe meetup with Biscuit, a coffee, and a cat, a perfect Thursday.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Biscuit approved by the Coffee Hunters. Keep the stories coming, Mariam ☕🐶

posts.author: p08
posts.text: Roaster shout-out: our new Ethiopian light roast is out this week, 250g bags sold at the counter. Come try a cup, tell us what you taste, and bring your own jar for a discount.

comments.author: p03
